Messages.Author: Xian
Messages.Body:
Just curious about the interaction of Sanguine Instruction and The Greatest
Trick. It'd be nifty if one could play SI, modifying it with TGT, to a
virtually guaranteed successful action, but there's something nagging me, saying
that it isn't doable. Probably something to do with the text on SI saying
something about "this acting vampire". If this isn't a roadblock, does SI
"require" a discipline, per TGT's card text, or does it just generically require
that a discipline be present on the vampire as it attempts an action?

Curious.

Xian

Messages.Author: Sander Hanevelt
Messages.Body:
<SNIP>
> So I guess the anwser is no.
>
> You cannot ever use them at the same time, since your vampire isn't a
> vampire anymore when he uses the grandest trick.

Forgot something, there is also something in the cardtext of the grandest
trick that states that you cannot use any cards that require a vampire, clan
or discipline.

So that makes it a definate no on your question.

Sorry about the messy postings, I was a bit sleepy.

Sander

Messages.Author: Sander Hanevelt
Messages.Body:
Previous post went wrong:

Sanguine Instruction
From the card text:
Requires a ready vampire. +1 stealth action

<omitted rest of card text>

The Grandest Trick
From the card text:
This acting vampire is treated as a mortal ally for the duration of the
action.

So I guess the anwser is no.

You cannot ever use them at the same time, since your vampire isn't a
vampire anymore when he uses the grandest trick.

Sander
